subject: Access provenance packet: service-account scoping + SCIM delta samples
messages:
From: Security Team <security@hearthline.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access provenance packet request for SOC2 intake

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for taking the intake call earlier. As part of our SOC 2 evidence collection for an upcoming audit, we need a compact "access provenance" packet focused on service accounts and SCIM delta behavior. Specifically we're asking for: 

- A snapshot of service-account owners and scopes (owner-of-record) for any non-human identities that access customer data (last 90 days).
- Representative SCIM delta exports demonstrating user lifecycle events (create/update/delete) and an explanation of how those deltas map to RBAC changes.
- One or two SAML assertion samples for an admin role (redacted PII) showing attributes used for role mapping.
- A brief attestation that least-privilege controls are in place for on-call/service-account escalation and the playbook for emergency access.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the above and an estimated delivery date? We are aiming to have artifacts uploaded to the intake folder by 2026-05-02.

Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (stub)

Regards,
Carlos Vega
Lead Security Analyst, Hearthline Medical
security@hearthline.com

---
Note: please treat the SCIM deltas as sensitive; we will need redaction guidance before public sharing.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <security@hearthline.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access provenance packet request for SOC2 intake

Carlos —

Appreciate the clear checklist. We can provide everything you listed. Quick summary of how we'll deliver: 

1) Service-account owner-of-record: CSV export (service-account-owner-map.csv) with columns: account_id, friendly_name, owner_email, owner_team, created_at, last_used_at, scopes. We will include an ownership attestation signed by the platform security lead.

2) SCIM deltas: a sample bundle (scim-delta-sample_2026-04-20.zip) containing 3 delta sequences covering joiner/offboarder/role-change workflows. Each file will have a small README that maps delta entries to actual RBAC effects in the platform.

3) SAML assertion examples: one admin and one read-only assertion (saml-assertion-example.txt). Both will be redacted for user identifiers; we'll keep the attribute set intact so you can verify mapping rules.

4) Least-privilege attestation & emergency access playbook: short memo outlining JITA (just-in-time admin) timeboxes, approval path, and audit logging retention.

Timeline: Irene will assemble the artifacts and run a quick redaction pass. Target: deliver signed packet to your Drive intake folder by 2026-04-28 EOD. If you need earlier access to any raw artifacts for triage, we can provide a controlled preview.

Questions for you: 
- Do you require the owner-of-record export to include last 12 months rather than 90 days?
- Are there any additional SAML attributes you specifically want shown (e.g., department, tenant_id)?

I'll loop Irene and Sean on next steps.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Manager, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Vega <security@hearthline.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access provenance packet request for SOC2 intake

Mina —

90 days is fine for the owner map; thanks for clarifying. For SAML attrs, department and tenant_id would be helpful.

One small ask on redaction: please keep a mapping file (internal-only) that records original identifiers to redacted placeholders so the auditor can follow the chain if needed — that file can remain off the shared intake folder and we will request it under NDA if required.

Also linking our DocuSign intake for artifact ingestion consent: https://docsign.example.com/r/HEARTH-3821

If you can make delivery 2026-04-28 as proposed that works. If you hit any blockers, let us know and we can schedule a 30-minute sync next week.

Best,
Carlos

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <security@hearthline.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access provenance packet request for SOC2 intake

Carlos —

Following up with the delivery plan. We completed generation and internal redaction review today. What we will upload to your intake folder (read-only share) on 2026-04-28: 

- scim-delta-sample_2026-04-20.zip (README inside maps deltas -> RBAC changes)
- service-account-owner-map.csv (90-day window)
- saml-assertion-example.txt (admin + de-identified)
- least-privilege-attestation.pdf (signed by Platform Security)
- redaction-guidance.txt (describes what was redacted and why)

Sensitive artifacts (originals and the identifier mapping) will be held in our secure evidence vault and can be shared under NDA if the auditor requires the full trail.

A few operational notes: 
- We've removed any long-lived plaintext secrets from the SCIM exports.
- For the owner_map, some service-accounts are owned by rotation teams; those are marked as owner_team=OnCall-Rotation with a point-of-contact.
- We'll include a short CSV of 'exemptions' explaining any service account with broader-than-usual scopes and the compensating controls.

If that looks good, we'll proceed to upload on schedule. Otherwise we can open a DocuSign consent request for the mapping file if you want auditor access before the audit.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
